library.name: Haplink
library.author: Connor McKelvey <Connormckelvey@utexas.edu>
library.sentence: Bidirectional serial communication protocol for haptic robotic devices
library.paragraph: Haplink provides a lightweight, real-time communication protocol between Arduino/embedded devices and host computers. Features parameter control, telemetry streaming, and type-safe data transfer with XOR checksum validation. Ideal for haptic feedback systems and robotics applications.

library.name: Keyhole
library.author: Jeremy Hill <jezhill@gmail.com>
library.sentence: A lightweight library for serial-port interaction: send commands and get/set sketch variables via a JSON- and Python-compatible text interface.
library.paragraph:
In one line, and usually with less than a microsecond of overhead, keyhole.variable("foo", foo); provides serial-port access to an integer, floating-point or String variable in your sketch. Set its value by sending foo=123
 - the variable() method will return true to let the sketch know when you do this. Query it by sending foo
 . Query all exposed variables at once by sending ?
 , or choose to have them auto-report themselves periodically. Responses are in easy-to-parse JSON format and can be turned into Python dicts with one call to ast.literal_eval(), but there's a plotter-compatibility mode too. For the computer's side of the interaction, a complementary Python module is included in the project repository (or available separately from PyPI with python -m pip install keyhole-comm[serial] ).
